assessment.intent: The article is focused: it tells service businesses to evaluate landing-page readiness, follow-up and lead quality before increasing Google Ads spend.
assessment.specificity: It gives concrete page choices, a decision table, a narrow public-form recommendation, a qualified-lead worksheet and an explicitly hypothetical cost-per-customer example without inventing client outcomes.
assessment.evidence: The factual claims stay close to the two cited sources: Google Analytics event tracking and W3C accessible-form guidance. No unsupported test results, percentages or client stories are added.
assessment.voice: The writing sounds like Michael: direct, practical, locally aware and willing to say that he would not automatically create a new landing page for every campaign.
assessment.usefulAsset: This is a useful pre-spend review page for Okanagan service businesses, especially when paired with a website or landing-page audit.
